gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.reported_symptom: Entering a You.com key and clicking 'Save key' did not result in You.com becoming CONFIGURED; the page kept showing 'You.com: NOT_CONFIGURED -- No API key configured for this provider.'
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.root_cause: A pure frontend bug in web/settings_search_providers.html. The Save-key click handler looked up its own input element LAZILY inside the click callback via row.querySelector('.p-key-input'). `row` is a DocumentFragment (template.content.cloneNode(true)); by click time, content.appendChild(row) (called once, at the end of render(), after every handler is wired) had already MOVED row's children into the live document, leaving the fragment empty. The lazy lookup returned null, and `input.value` threw an uncaught TypeError BEFORE the API call was ever made -- so .env was never written and no error was ever shown (the exception happened before the try/catch). Confirmed directly via a real Playwright session (page.on('pageerror') captured the exact TypeError) and via a parallel curl diagnostic proving the BACKEND was already correct all along (write + os.environ update + immediate GET reflecting configured:true, same process, no restart).
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.exact_fix: Capture the input element reference ONCE at render time (const keyInput = row.querySelector('.p-key-input'), evaluated before appendChild moves the fragment's children) and reference that captured variable inside the click handler instead of re-querying the now-empty `row`.
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.second_gap_closed: search_provider_adapter.SearchProviderAdapterBase gained an __init__ that sets an INSTANCE-level `status` (AdapterStatus.ENABLED if get_configured_providers() else NOT_ENABLED), recomputed fresh on every construction. source_registry.get_adapter(source) always constructs a fresh instance, so discover_from_sources()'s pre-flight gate now picks up a newly-saved key on the very next real search run, no restart -- without touching the class-level `.status` other code (source_capabilities.py's generic helper, source_registry.get_adapter_status()) still reads for every other adapter.
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.save_test: scripts/test_phase14_2_hot_refresh.py: saving a fake key makes is_provider_configured('you') True in the same process immediately; SearchProviderManager.eligible_providers() and a freshly-constructed adapter's own .status both confirm ENABLED right after -- no restart.
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.remove_test: Same file: removing the key immediately flips is_provider_configured('you') back to False; SearchProviderManager immediately excludes it; a freshly-constructed adapter's .status immediately reads NOT_ENABLED again.
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.provider_manager_refresh_test: Replacing a fake key three times in a row proved the VERY NEXT SearchProviderManager.search() call always sees the current value -- no cached provider instance anywhere in the construction path.
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.api_immediacy_test: Via a real FastAPI TestClient: GET /api/settings/search-providers shows configured:true immediately after POST .../key; GET /api/sources shows search_provider_status=AVAILABLE, search_provider=YOU, final_status=AVAILABLE_VIA_SEARCH_PROVIDER for every restricted board immediately after, and reverts immediately after DELETE .../key -- no restart in either direction.
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.browser_smoke_test: Real Chromium (Playwright) session against the live dev server with a fake key: NOT_CONFIGURED -> entered key -> Save -> page state reload -> CONFIGURED (bug fixed, previously stayed NOT_CONFIGURED) -> raw key never appeared in page HTML -> Remove -> back to NOT_CONFIGURED. Zero uncaught page errors (previously the exact TypeError).
gui_provider_key_hot_refresh_fix.incident_disclosure: This browser smoke test discovered the real project .env already contained the user's genuine You.com API key (evidently saved through a means outside the broken GUI). The smoke test's own Remove-key step, run against the shared live dev server, deleted that real key as an unintended side effect of testing the removal flow. It was recovered from this session's own prior diagnostic output and restored via the real POST .../key endpoint (confirmed via GET .../search-providers: configured:true, masked value ending in the same last 4 characters as the original). All further destructive UI testing in this fix used an isolated .env copy exclusively.
